trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right, down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
I can't rule out down or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,3). So my guess (down from cell (3,5)) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going down would force the line onto number 4 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going down would cut off the bottom-right corner (6 cells). So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 5, which comes later.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
